summary: Fire tower erected in 1930 in Amherst, Laurentides, restored and owned by the municipality; a free trail leads to it, but climbing is forbidden.

access.note: The trail and site are open and free; the register says the public may not climb the tower, and a visitor account says climbing is forbidden.

visit.trail_note: About 1.5 km trail from chemin Saint-Louis, maintained by the municipality; a visitor account gives May to November as the access period.

events.note: Erected in 1930 per the register; the Quebec heritage record gives 1930 as the construction date
Bought by the municipality, according to a visitor account
Restored by the municipality, which took ownership, per the register; a visitor account gives 1996 for the restoration
Listed in the Laurentides MRC heritage inventory (2013), recorded in the Quebec heritage register (RPCQ 196596)
Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register as CAN 11, QC 1

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a restoration by the municipality in 1997. A visitor account gives a purchase in 1987 and a restoration in 1996. The story gives the register's date and mentions the other account.

The register names the owner as the Saint-Remi-d'Amherst Municipality. The municipality's own page is titled Municipalité d'Amherst, and the Quebec heritage record lists the municipality as Amherst. These appear to be the same municipal body under two names.

sources.title: Tour à feu
sources.publisher: Répertoire du patrimoine culturel du Québec (Ministère de la Culture et des Communications)

notes_for_editor: Built year (1930) agrees across the register, the Quebec heritage record and a trail guide. Restoration dates disagree: the register says restored in 1997 by the municipality, which took ownership; the visitor account says bought in 1987 and restored in 1996. The story reports both. The owner name differs: the register says Saint-Remi-d'Amherst Municipality, while the municipality's site says Municipalité d'Amherst and the RPCQ record says Amherst. The agency field was left as the record has it for a human to decide. Elevation also differs: the register gives 1,282 ft (391 m); the trail guide describes the site as about 200 m altitude and lists a maximum of 670 m, so no elevation is stated. Climbing: the register and the visitor account both say the tower may not be climbed. A search snippet for a second visitor page (Passion Chalets) mentions 700 steps to the tower, but that page was not read and is not used. No design, staffing, fire or cab information appears in the sources read, so none is stated. The register's photo credit (William Haddad) was not added to photos.
